edges.description: Neutrophilic infiltration and vessel-wall destruction manifest histologically as leukocytoclastic necrotizing vasculitis with fibrinoid necrosis.
Dermal postcapillary venule leukocytoclastic vasculitis causes erythrocyte extravasation and palpable purpura.
Severe cutaneous small- and medium-vessel vasculitis leads to ischemic tissue breakdown and skin ulceration.
Cutaneous small-vessel inflammation and partial microvascular obstruction produce livedo reticularis.
Systemic immune-complex vascular inflammation drives constitutional asthenia and fatigue as part of Meltzer triad.
Immune-complex synovial and microvascular inflammation produces arthralgia.
Immune-complex articular inflammation manifests clinically as non-erosive arthritis.
Vasa nervorum small-vessel vasculitis causes ischemic axonal injury and peripheral neuropathy.
Renal glomerular cryoglobulin deposition and inflammatory injury cause membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis.
Intravascular cryoprotein gelation increases plasma viscosity and manifests clinically as hyperviscosity syndrome.
Cold-induced cryoprotein precipitation and microvascular vasospasm/occlusion in acral vessels produce Raynaud phenomenon.
Cold-induced cutaneous microvascular occlusion causes ischemic necrosis and acral skin ulceration.
Partial obstruction of cutaneous microvascular blood flow by cryoprecipitates produces livedo reticularis.
Chronic HCV infection provides sustained viral stimulation of B cells, promoting expansion of pathogenic cryoglobulin-producing B-cell clones.
